personal.name: Manash Swain
personal.role: Full-Stack Software Engineer & AI Workflow Specialist
taglines: I don't just write syntax—I design resilient systems.
Building performant web applications, clean REST APIs, and agentic AI workflows.
From solving 300+ DSA problems to architecting secure LLM pipelines.
about: I am a passionate Full-Stack Software Developer currently pursuing a BS in Computer Science at BITS Pilani (2024 - 2027). I specialize in creating clean, maintainable web applications and solving complex algorithmic challenges.

My journey started with a deep curiosity for how things work under the hood. Whether I'm optimizing a SQL database query with CTEs, designing a Kanban dashboard, or practicing core computer science concepts (like the 300+ problems I've solved across LeetCode and GeeksforGeeks), I love the endless learning loop that development offers.

Recently, I've been fascinated by AI Automation and Agentic Workflows. I'm exploring how to build robust LLM pipelines with Anthropic's Claude API, focusing on tool use, structured outputs (Pydantic), and implementing rule-based gating (like ensuring a model never has final authority over a financial transaction).

projects.title: TaskFlow
projects.short_description: A full-stack task management application with real-time analytics and Kanban boards.
projects.problem: Teams often struggle to track project progress visually without feeling overwhelmed by complex enterprise tools.
projects.architecture: Client-side state managed by React, synchronized with an Express/MongoDB backend. Uses JWT for secure session management.
projects.key_challenge: Implementing smooth drag-and-drop Kanban functionality while ensuring optimistic UI updates synced flawlessly with backend state.
projects.solution: Built a robust state synchronization layer in React that locally updates the board instantly, falling back gracefully if the API request fails.
projects.outcome: A seamless, zero-latency feel for the user with robust data persistence.
projects.reflection: If I rebuilt this today, I'd implement WebSockets for true multi-player collaboration instead of standard HTTP polling.

projects.title: Gatekeeper (Agentic AI System)
projects.short_description: A secure AI agent workflow implementing strict rule-based gating for sensitive actions.
projects.problem: Fully autonomous LLM agents are prone to hallucination. Giving them direct access to execute critical actions (like payments or DB deletes) is a massive security risk.
projects.architecture: A multi-layered agent system where the LLM can *propose* actions via Tool Use, but a deterministic rules-engine acts as a 'Gatekeeper' that validates all parameters before execution.
projects.key_challenge: Ensuring the LLM outputs structured, perfectly formatted data that the rule engine could parse without crashing.
projects.solution: Utilized Anthropic's Claude API with strict Pydantic schemas to force structured JSON outputs, combined with a retry-loop for self-correction.
projects.outcome: Achieved 0% hallucinated execution rate on critical actions.
projects.reflection: The architecture choice ('model never has final authority over a money action') proved that combining deterministic code with probabilistic AI yields the safest production systems.

projects.title: Socially
projects.short_description: A private organizational social network with restricted department-level channels.
projects.problem: Organizations need a secure, internal way to share updates without relying on chaotic email threads or public social media.
projects.architecture: React frontend heavily integrated with Supabase for backend-as-a-service (BaaS), utilizing Row Level Security (RLS) policies.
projects.key_challenge: Designing a database schema that strictly enforced viewing permissions based on a user's department and role.
projects.solution: Leveraged Supabase's PostgreSQL RLS policies to ensure that users could only query posts belonging to their authorized channels at the database level.
projects.outcome: A highly secure, performant feed that scales effortlessly.
projects.reflection: Using Supabase taught me the power of pushing security down to the database layer rather than handling it all in the application logic.

projects.title: DataPulse: Sales Insights
projects.short_description: An end-to-end data analytics dashboard analyzing customer acquisition and cohort behaviors.
projects.problem: Raw sales data is noisy and difficult for non-technical stakeholders to interpret for strategic decisions.
projects.architecture: Jupyter Notebook environment performing heavy data cleaning with Pandas, followed by statistical visualization with Seaborn.
projects.key_challenge: Handling missing values and outliers in a massive dataset without skewing the overall cohort retention metrics.
projects.solution: Applied sophisticated imputation techniques and generated multi-variable distribution plots to isolate true behavioral trends.
projects.outcome: Actionable insights that clearly visualize drop-off points in the customer lifecycle.
projects.reflection: I realized that the hardest part of data analytics isn't the code—it's asking the right questions before you start plotting.
